message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (titled *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the Harry Potter series; introduced the world of Hogwarts. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; follows Harry’s return to school and the mystery of the Chamber. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry’s interference. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s past and the Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Final book; concludes the epic battle between good and evil. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 (book) / 2016 (film) | Companion guide to magical creatures; later adapted into a film series. |
| **Quidditch Through the Ages** | 2001 | A humorous look at the history of Quidditch. |
| **The Tales of Beedle the Bard** | 2008 | Collection of wizarding fairy tales. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; explores social issues in a small town. |

These titles have sold millions worldwide and have been translated into dozens of languages. If you’re interested in her other works—such as the Cormoran Strike detective novels published under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith—I’d be happy to list those too!
